text_blocks.snippet: If you test positive for COVID-19, you should isolate yourself from others, monitor your symptoms, and seek medical care if you have risk factors for severe illness or experience emergency warning signs. Treatment, if started within a few days of symptom onset, may help reduce the severity and duration of illness.

list.snippet: Assume you have COVID-19: A positive test result indicates the presence of the virus, meaning you have or recently had an infection.
Isolate: Stay home and away from others to prevent the spread of the virus.
Monitor symptoms: Pay attention to any symptoms you experience and their severity.
Seek medical care: If you have risk factors for severe illness or experience emergency warning signs, seek medical care immediately.
Treatment: If started early, treatment can help manage symptoms and shorten the duration of illness, according to the CDC.

text_blocks.snippet: People with COVID-19 are typically contagious for an average of 8 days, but the duration can vary. While the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) previously recommended 10 days of isolation, they now advise that individuals can end isolation after 5 days if their symptoms are improving and they wear a mask for the remaining 5 days. Factors like underlying health conditions and the severity of illness can also influence the length of contagiousness. NAAT (nucleic acid amplification tests) can remain positive for longer than antigen tests, even after the infectious period has passed according to the CDC.

text_blocks.snippet: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends several measures to prevent the spread of COVID-19. These include staying home when sick and away from others, seeking prompt medical care for testing and treatment, especially for those at higher risk of severe illness, and considering vaccination to stay up-to-date.

list.title: Stay home when sick:
list.snippet: If you have respiratory symptoms, stay home and away from others, including those you live with, until you are no longer contagious.

list.title: Seek testing and treatment:
list.snippet: If you are at higher risk of severe illness, seek medical care promptly for testing and/or treatment, which may reduce the risk of severe illness if started within a few days of symptom onset.
The CDC recommends a 2024-2025 COVID-19 vaccine for most adults ages 18 and older.
Parents should also consider vaccination for children ages 6 months and older.
Keep up-to-date with the latest recommendations and get vaccinated when eligible.
The CDC is continually updating its recommendations, including vaccine recommendations.
The CDC's recommendations for when to return to normal activities are based on individual circumstances and symptom resolution.
